chunks: One is the scholar and divine; then the seeker of knowledge who is also on the way to deliverance. Then (lastly) the common rot who run after every caller and bend in the direction of every wind. They seek no light from the effulgence of knowledge and do not take protection of any reliable support.

key_terms.رَبَّانِيٌّ: Divine scholar; one who possesses deep, divinely-inspired knowledge
key_terms.رَعَاعٌ: The lowest or most insignificant part of a people; scum
key_terms.هَمَجٌ: Common people; those lacking refinement or distinct character

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) categorizes humanity into three distinct groups based on their relationship with knowledge and stability: the learned scholars, the seekers of salvation, and the ignorant masses who follow every trend without firm grounding. This tripartite division, found in Nahj al-Balagha, reflects the Shia emphasis on *'ilm* (knowledge) as the primary criterion for spiritual hierarchy, contrasting the steadfastness of the *Rabbaniyyun* with the fickleness of the *Hamaj* (the unrefined crowd). The description of the third group highlights their lack of *nur al-'ilm* (light of knowledge), serving as a warning against blind following (*taqlid*) in matters of faith and practice.
